2021.title: Ida Drenches Connecticut, Causes Major Flooding

response_agencies: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
event.summary: The remnants of Hurricane Ida caused massive flooding in Connecticut from Wednesday into early Thursday, stranding vehicles in parts of the state and forcing rescues from homes in Plainville. The storm dumped several inches of rain in parts of the state, causing major flooding on streets and river levels to rise to dangerous levels. Some towns saw seven to eight inches of rain since Wednesday morning. Water levels around the state are very high, so there is a possibility of strong currents and hazardous debris in rivers and streams. Gillette Castle State Park in East Haddam and Indian Well State Park in Shelton are closed because of storm damage. Dozens of schools across Connecticut delayed opening or closed for the day Thursday due to the ongoing flooding issues and damage left by Ida. The Connecticut Department of Transportation is responding to damage Ida caused on state roads, culverts and bridges. In Plainville, 18 people were rescued from homes on Forestville Avenue overnight. Several roads in Plainville were impassable. Metro-North suspended service on all lines late Wednesday night due to the severe weather and said it expected service to stay out overnight due to flooding and power outages. Police in Fairfield County were warning of road closures due to flooding and asking people not to travel unless it is an emergency. As of midnight, Bridgeport emergency officials were reporting 17 locations with vehicles stranded or submerged by floodwaters, and at least 22 streets flooded. In Norwalk, multiple streets were closed due to flooding. Fairfield police described scenes of multiple vehicles stuck or submerged on flooded roadways. From 7 p.m Wednesday to 6 a.m. Thursday, Fairfield Police Department responded to 40 flooding condition calls with approximately 30 vehicles towed due to road conditions, 13 road hazards and two motor vehicle crashes. Up to eight and a half inches of rain fell in Stamford. The mayor's office said that by 10 a.m., city emergency management officials had responded to 17 motor vehicle crashes, flooded buildings, more than 600 power outages, and 18 water rescues. Officials in Darien reported flooding and multiple trouble spots Wednesday night. As of 4 a.m., Eversource was reporting more than 21,500 outages and United Illuminating was reporting more than 16,000.

2022.title: Flooding in Thanh Hoa, Nghệ An, Hà Tĩnh killed eight people

locs: Mường Xén to Tây Sơn line

event.response_agencies: Standing Office of the National Directorate for Disaster Prevention
event.summary: Flooding in the provinces of Thanh Hoa, Nghệ An, Hà Tĩnh has killed 8 people. Floodwaters caused 26 houses to be damaged by over 70%; 143 houses damaged, roofs splayed; 55 houses affected by landslides; more than 2,000 homes evacuated; 14,033 houses flooded. Floodwaters also produced 11,435 hectares of rice, colorful flowers; more than 3,800 hectares of industrial, annual, perennial fruit trees; nearly 135 hectares of forest; over 9,000 hectares of ponds; more than 710 tons of salt damaged; 155,340 livestock, poultry killed, drifted; 127 school sites affected; 9,150 m of ditch; 26 small dam dam damaged; 82 bridges, damaged; 1,550 m of river bank washed away; over 75,800 m3 of rock flooded; 112 sewers damaged; 29 sites flooded; 100 sites washed away; 51 power poles, over 5,500 m of fence collapsed. In particular in Ky Son district, Nghệ An province, this is the area that was heavily damaged by the flooding, as of 17:30 on 2 October, 14 houses were washed away (Tac Chau, Mường Xen town); 85 houses in Ta Chau commune and Mường Xen town; flooded State agencies in Block 1, Mường Xen town. Currently, the water has receded, leaving mud, filling the soil; 19 houses were washed away, including 3 strong houses completely washed away (in the city of Cang, Sơn Hà); completely collapsed the workhouse of the Ta Cạ Public Security Society. Several sections of the Mường Xén to Tây Sơn line (including 4 very heavy landslides), damaged the iron arch bridge of Hòa Sơn, Ta Cạ commune. Traffic to the towns of Ta Chau and Ti Sơn was completely jammed; the road was diverted to the 7th national highway at Ta Chau, where vehicles are currently unable to pass; the road was diverted to 10 points on the 7th national highway in the area of Nậm Cắn. In addition, the floodwater isolated two communes, including Hòa Sơn, which had a population of 236 and 966 people, and Sơn Hà, which was completely isolated; two cars were washed away (one was rescued); 10 cars were flooded.
